sets.relationshipLabel: common name leading to its technical name
sets.explanation: A string puppet is popularly called a marionette, and a hand puppet is popularly called a glove puppet — each pair moves from the everyday label to its more specific technical one.
baitTags: glove puppet now lives only here, resolving the earlier overlap with the concealment set
ordering now has a clear direction: common term first, technical term second

sets.relationshipLabel: the worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A carver works with a chisel just as a marionettist works with a control bar — each craftsperson is defined by the tool in their hand.
baitTags: marionettist echoes marionette from the synonymity set

sets.relationshipLabel: the start and finish of shaping a carved piece
sets.explanation: A rough-cut is finished by a polish and a sketch is finished by a sculpture — both pairs track the first rough attempt through to the same object's completed form.
baitTags: polish and finished sculpture both read as 'the finished thing', tempting a mismatched cross-pair swap

sets.relationshipLabel: the covering that hides the true thing beneath it
sets.explanation: Blacks are worn to hide the puppeteer from the audience's eye, just as a mask hides the face beneath it — in both pairs the visible cover conceals the real thing underneath.
baitTags: blacks reads like ordinary clothing vocabulary before its concealing function clicks
mask/face no longer shares roots with any puppet-type name, closing the old glove/hand loophole
